findings.text: blocking: the landed removal of _reuse_covered's third element leaves this file's own mutation arms unpacking a value that is gone. Its _KEEP_REMOVED arm binds 'covered, dirs, scanned = result' at line 120 and returns a three-tuple at line 131, and its _ALL_OR_NOTHING arm indexes 'result[2]' at line 149; at head _reuse_covered returns two elements, so arming either control raises before the mutation is exercised. Reproduced in this review with RECKON_TEST_RESCAN_KEEP_REMOVED=1 at a1c0780f2: 'ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 3, got 2)' at tests/test_a_changed_directory_rescans_only_itself.py:120, 5 failed. The unarmed file passes (it is absent from the failure list of the head population), so the arm's whole signal is the unpack error rather than the case the control is declared for, and the guard that keeps a vanished directory's files out of the covered set can no longer be shown to fire. The repair is a few lines in a file outside this node's fence, so it cannot be made here; nothing else in the diff owns it.

follow-on: this arm's own header names the revision it ran at as 'e05213f40 + dirty worktree', while the manifest's after_suite (manifest.md line 18) records that same run's revision as '781c01879'. Both describe one gate, and the commit was made from that dirty tree four minutes later, but nothing recorded shows the two trees are identical, so a reader comparing the receipt against the log it cites finds a revision the log does not name. The counts are not in doubt (1 failed, 165 passed in this log, 3 failed, 159 passed in gate-base.log, no added failure id); only the revision the receipt stands on is asserted rather than shown.
